mainTopic: Whether causing benefit (מהנה) to עבודה זרה is forbidden: ריש לקיש vs. רבי יוחנן, רבי נתן's ברייתא, buying at a gentile fair, and the details of destroying a forbidden animal.
overview: The amud asks whether it is forbidden only to get benefit from עבודה זרה (נהנה), or also to give it benefit (מהנה). ריש לקיש allows giving benefit. רבי יוחנן forbids it with a קל וחומר. The גמרא challenges ריש לקיש from a ברייתא of רבי נתן. In that ברייתא, a Jew facing an idol's tax break is trapped between benefiting and causing benefit, so goods from an idol's market must be destroyed. רב משרשיא answers that ריש לקיש follows the רבנן, who argue with רבי נתן, while רבי יוחנן holds they agree. A ברייתא that allows buying at a gentile fair seems to prove they argue. On the way, it teaches when a כהן may become impure to go to court, to learn תורה, or to marry, and the הלכה follows רבי יוסי. רבי יוחנן's side answers that רבי נתן speaks of a merchant who pays the idol's tax, and the other ברייתא of a homeowner who does not. The גמרא then defends the rule of maiming the animal against צער בעלי חיים, and begins comparing it with a ברייתא about הקדש nowadays, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: causing benefit is allowed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש finishes his statement: only getting benefit from עבודה זרה is forbidden, while giving it benefit is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But causing benefit is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes ריש לקיש's opinion from just before. Shops decorated with fruit for the idol are allowed, because the shopper gets no benefit from them; he only helps the idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש separates two things: נהנה (you enjoy something from the idol) and מהנה (you give the idol some gain). In his view only the first is forbidden. So buying from a fruit-decorated shop, which only helps the idol, is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Causing benefit; giving gain to someone else (here, to the idol)
Deriving benefit; getting enjoyment for yourself

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two similar words. נֶהֱנֶה means YOU get the benefit. מְהַנֶּה means you GIVE the benefit to the idol. The whole סוגיא depends on keeping them apart.

phrases.english: but causing benefit is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's statement from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only deriving benefit (נהנה) from עבודה זרה is forbidden; causing benefit (מהנה) to it is permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: causing benefit is surely forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says even fruit-decorated shops are forbidden, because of a קל וחומר: causing benefit is worse than getting benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן says: even shops decorated with fruit are forbidden. This follows from a קל וחומר: if deriving benefit is forbidden, then causing benefit is all the more so forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן argues with ריש לקיש and forbids even the fruit-decorated shops. He proves it with a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש allowed מהנה. רבי יוחנן says helping the idol is even worse than enjoying something from it. So if נהנה is forbidden, מהנה must be forbidden too. That makes fruit-decorated shops forbidden as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan says:
Even if they are decorated with fruit, it is also forbidden,
phrases.notes: "They" means the shops decorated in the idol's honor.

phrases.english: a kal vachomer: deriving benefit is forbidden,
causing benefit, all the more so!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with ריש לקיש and forbids מהנה too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Causing benefit to עבודה זרה is forbidden, a fortiori from the ban on deriving benefit, so even fruit-decorated shops are forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge from Rabbi Natan: the idol's tax break
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי נתן: on the idol's day, the tax is dropped for anyone who wears a wreath in the idol's honor.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection. רבי נתן says: On a day when idol worship lets off the tax, they announce and say: Anyone who takes a wreath and puts it on his head and on his donkey's head in honor of the idol will have his tax dropped. If not, his tax will not be dropped.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge ריש לקיש. This step only sets up the case; the challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here is the case: a tax break is given only to people who honor the idol with a wreath. Anyone who doesn't wear one pays the full tax. That puts a Jew into a tricky spot, which the next line spells out.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Natan says:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם שֶׁעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מַנַּחַת בּוֹ אֶת הַמֶּכֶס,
phrases.english: On a day when idol worship lets off the tax,
phrases.notes: Literally "leaves the tax": in the idol's honor, the tax is lowered or dropped that day.

phrases.english: they announce and say:
Anyone who takes a wreath
and places it on his head and on his donkey's head
in honor of the idol,
they will let him off the tax,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם לָאו — אַל יַנִּיחַ לוֹ אֶת הַמֶּכֶס.
phrases.english: and if not, they will not let him off the tax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a ברייתא that will be used against ריש לקיש's leniency.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that מהנה is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא will treat paying the idol's tax (מהנה) as a problem, just like taking the tax break (נהנה).

steps.title: The Jew's dilemma: benefiting or causing benefit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what a Jew there should do. Wearing the wreath means benefiting; not wearing it means causing benefit.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew who is there, what should he do? If he puts on the wreath, he turns out to be benefiting. If he doesn't, he turns out to be causing benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the heart of the challenge. The ברייתא treats both choices as forbidden, including מהנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the Jew wears the wreath, he gets the tax break from the idol, which is נהנה. If he refuses, he pays a tax that honors the idol, which is מהנה. The ברייתא calls this a real problem, which goes against ריש לקיש, who said מהנה is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He turns out to be; he ends up

steps.whyThisMatters: This line shows that the ברייתא considers מהנה forbidden, which supports רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: A Jew who is there, what should he do?
If he places it, he turns out to be deriving benefit,
phrases.notes: "It" is the wreath. Wearing it gets him the tax break.

phrases.english: if he does not place it, he turns out to be causing benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the dilemma out of the tax case and shows that מהנה is treated as forbidden.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's claim that מהנה is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If מהנה were permitted, the Jew could simply refuse the wreath and pay the tax, and there would be no dilemma.

steps.title: Ruling: destroy what was bought in an idol's market
steps.stepSummary: From this, the ברייתא rules that whatever is bought in an idol's market must be destroyed, each type of item in its own way.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: One who does business in a market of idol worship: an animal must be crippled; fruit, clothing and utensils must be left to rot; money and metal utensils he should take to the Dead Sea.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא draws a practical rule from the dilemma: goods from an idol's market are forbidden and must be gotten rid of.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing business there always involves benefiting from the idol or helping it. So the goods may not be used at all. Things that rot are left to rot, and things that never rot, like money and metal, are thrown into ים המלח.
steps.whatToRemember: An idol's market is so tied to עבודה זרה that its goods must be destroyed completely, with no benefit taken from them at all.

phrases.english: From here they said:

phrases.aramaic: הַנּוֹשֵׂא וְנוֹתֵן בְּשׁוּק שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה,
phrases.english: One who does business in a market of idol worship,
an animal must be crippled,
fruit, clothing and utensils must rot,
money and metal utensils,
he should take them to the Dead Sea,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the dilemma into a practical ruling within the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Goods bought in an idol's market are forbidden and must be destroyed.

steps.title: How is an animal crippled?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what counts as the עיקור of an animal that it just required.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is crippling?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a clarifying question about the word תֵּיעָקֵר. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling us to "cripple" the animal is not exact enough. We need to know the specific action that counts.

phrases.english: And what is crippling?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term used in the ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exact action counts as crippling the animal.

steps.title: Cutting the hooves below the knee
steps.stepSummary: Crippling means cutting off the animal's hooves from the knee joint down.
steps.simpleTranslation: One cuts off its hooves from the knee and below.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: you cut the animal's legs from the knee downward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting the legs below the knee makes the animal useless for work. This is how the animal is "destroyed."

phrases.english: One who cuts off its hooves
from the knee and below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the definition of עיקור.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עיקור means cutting the hooves from the knee joint downward.

steps.title: The punchline: the ברייתא forbids causing benefit too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the words of the ברייתא that show that causing benefit to the idol is also a problem. This challenges ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any event, the ברייתא teaches: if he puts on the wreath, he is benefiting from the idol; if he doesn't, he is causing benefit to the idol!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states the point of the long ברייתא it just quoted. The ברייתא treats causing benefit to an idol as something to worry about, and that goes against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts the Jew in a trap. Wearing the wreath means benefiting, and not wearing it means causing benefit, because he would then pay the tax that goes to the idol. If causing benefit were allowed, the ברייתא would have no trap at all. So causing benefit must also be forbidden, and ריש לקיש allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: In any event, it teaches. This points to the key words of a source quoted for a challenge.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up נֶהֱנֶה (getting benefit) with מְהַנֶּה (giving benefit). The whole argument here is only about מְהַנֶּה.

phrases.english: In any event, it teaches:
If he places it, he is found to be benefiting;
phrases.notes: "It" means the wreath worn in the idol's honor, from רבי נתן's case.

phrases.english: if he does not place it, he is found to be causing benefit!
phrases.notes: If he doesn't wear it, he pays the tax, and that money helps the idol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in steps 3-7
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that causing benefit to עבודה זרה is allowed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא sees not wearing the wreath (which causes benefit) as a problem. So causing benefit must be forbidden.

steps.title: ריש לקיש follows the רבנן who argue with רבי נתן
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא answers that ריש לקיש holds the רבנן disagree with רבי נתן, and he follows the רבנן. רבי יוחנן holds there is no disagreement.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא son of רב אידי said: ריש לקיש holds that the רבנן argue with רבי נתן, and he ruled like those רבנן. רבי יוחנן holds that they do not argue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא defends ריש לקיש. He says the ברייתא only gives רבי נתן's opinion, and the רבנן disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge came from רבי נתן, so it only works if everyone agrees with him. ריש לקיש is said to hold that the רבנן argue, so he can side with them. רבי יוחנן holds that everyone agrees with רבי נתן, which explains why he forbids causing benefit.
steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the debate. The question is no longer whether causing benefit is allowed. It becomes whether the רבנן really argue with רבי נתן, and the next steps test exactly that.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya son of Rav Idi said:
Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish holds:
The Rabbis disagree with Rabbi Natan,
and I spoke in accordance with the Rabbis who disagree with him.
phrases.notes: This is said as if ריש לקיש himself were speaking: "I ruled like the רבנן."

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan holds: they do not disagree.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the challenging source to one side of a מחלוקת
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא of רבי נתן seemed to be what everyone holds.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is only רבי נתן's view. The רבנן argue, and ריש לקיש follows them. רבי יוחנן says there is no argument.

steps.title: Challenge: a ברייתא allows buying at a gentile fair
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the רבנן really don't argue. It quotes a ברייתא that allows going to a gentile fair to buy animals, slaves, and land, and registering the deeds in gentile courts.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they don't argue? But a ברייתא teaches: one may go to a gentile fair and buy animals, slaves, maidservants, houses, fields, and vineyards from them. He may write the deeds and have them confirmed in their courts, because it is like rescuing the property from their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's claim that the רבנן agree with רבי נתן. It starts quoting a ברייתא that allows trading at an idol's fair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An idol's fair is exactly the kind of place where buying helps the idol. Yet this ברייתא allows it. That seems to show that some תנאים do not forbid causing benefit, so the רבנן would argue with רבי נתן. The גמרא spells out this point in step 18, after finishing the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא? This brings a source to challenge something.
A fair or market, here one held in honor of an idol
Like rescuing it from their hands

phrases.english: And they do not disagree?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
One may go to a fair of gentiles,
and buy from them an animal,
slaves and maidservants,
houses, fields, and vineyards,
and he may write and confirm deeds in their courts,
because it is as though he is rescuing it from their hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim at the end of step 9 that the רבנן do not disagree
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the רבנן agree with רבי נתן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא allows buying at an idol's fair, which seems to allow causing benefit. So some must disagree with רבי נתן.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: a כהן may become impure to go to court
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא adds that a כהן may become impure by going outside ארץ ישראל, or even into a cemetery, to go to court and argue against gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he is a כהן, he may become impure by going outside ארץ ישראל to go to court and argue against them. And just as he may become impure outside ארץ ישראל, so may he become impure in a cemetery.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא from the last step. It adds a ruling about a כהן who needs to deal with gentiles over property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a כהן must avoid טומאה, including the impurity of land outside ארץ ישראל and of a cemetery. The ברייתא allows him to do both so he can go to court and protect his claim. This shows how far the ברייתא goes to let a Jew get property back from gentiles.

keyTerms.meaning: To go to court and to contest a claim

phrases.english: And if he was a priest,
he may become impure by going outside the Land,
to litigate and contest with them.
And just as he may become impure outside the Land,
so he may become impure in a cemetery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא that was brought as a challenge in step 10
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's view that the רבנן agree with רבי נתן (the challenge is still being built)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This is the rest of the challenging ברייתא. The גמרא states its punchline in step 18.

steps.title: A cemetery? That impurity is from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops in the middle of the ברייתא and asks how a כהן could be allowed into a real cemetery, since that טומאה is a Torah law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really think it means a cemetery? That impurity is from the Torah!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts its quote of the ברייתא. It is surprised that the ברייתא lets a כהן enter a cemetery.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of a cemetery for a כהן is a Torah prohibition. The רבנן cannot simply permit a Torah prohibition so that a כהן can argue a court case. So the plain reading of the ברייתא seems impossible.

keyTerms.meaning: Can it enter your mind? (an expression of surprise)

phrases.english: In a cemetery — can it enter your mind?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 11, where the ברייתא said a כהן may even enter a cemetery to go to court.

phrases.english: It is an impurity from the Torah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the last line of the ברייתא quoted in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's words that a כהן may enter a cemetery.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cemetery impurity is a Torah law, and the רבנן cannot permit a Torah prohibition for a court case.

steps.title: It means a field of doubtful graves, impure only by the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is really talking about a בית הפרס, whose impurity is only from the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means a בית הפרס, which is impure only by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question. The 'cemetery' in the ברייתא is really a בית הפרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הפרס is a field where a grave was plowed over, so bones may be scattered there. Its impurity is only מדרבנן. Since the רבנן made that rule, they can relax it for an important need like fighting gentiles in court.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed over, so it is unclear where the bones are
From the רבנן (rabbinic law), not from the Torah

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not allowing a כהן to break a Torah prohibition. The leniency only covers a rabbinic impurity.

phrases.english: Rather, it means a field of doubtful graves, which is impure only by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulty raised in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: 'cemetery' means a בית הפרס.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows entering a real cemetery, which is Torah-level impurity.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא allows only a בית הפרס, which is rabbinic-level impurity and can be relaxed.

steps.title: A כהן may leave the Land to learn or marry; רבי יהודה limits this
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a כהן may become impure by leaving ארץ ישראל to learn תורה or to marry. רבי יהודה says this applies only if he has nowhere to learn in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן may also become impure to learn תורה or to marry a woman. רבי יהודה said: When? When he cannot find a place to learn. But when he can find a place to learn, he may not become impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא. It lists two more reasons a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל, and רבי יהודה adds a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Land outside ארץ ישראל was made impure by the רבנן, so a כהן normally should not go there. Learning תורה and getting married are important enough to allow it. רבי יהודה says learning is a valid reason only when he truly cannot learn at home.

keyTerms.meaning: He finds a place or teacher to learn from

phrases.english: And he may become impure to learn Torah and to marry a woman.
phrases.notes: He becomes impure by leaving ארץ ישראל, the same way as in step 11.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: When does this apply?
When he cannot find a place to learn.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹצֵא לִלְמוֹד — אֵינוֹ מְטַמֵּא.
phrases.english: But when he can find a place to learn, he may not become impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side question about the cemetery, the גמרא resumes quoting the ברייתא from steps 10-11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה or to marry. According to רבי יהודה, he may leave to learn only if he cannot learn in ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי יוסי allows it even when there is a place to learn
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees: a כהן may leave even if he could learn in ארץ ישראל, because not every person succeeds in learning from every teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: Even when he can find a place to learn, he may become impure, because a person does not merit to learn from everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings רבי יוסי, who argues with רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוסי, it is not enough that some teacher exists in ארץ ישראל. The right teacher for this student may live outside the Land, so going to him counts as a real need for learning.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that finding the right teacher matters, not just having a teacher available.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
Even when he can find a place to learn, he may become impure,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָדָם זוֹכֶה לִלְמוֹד מִכֹּל.
phrases.english: because a person does not merit to learn from everyone.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ בִּזְמַן שֶׁמּוֹצֵא לִלְמוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's limitation in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה even if teachers are available there.

steps.title: The story of יוסף הכהן who followed his teacher to צידון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי supports his view with a story: יוסף הכהן followed his teacher to צידון, outside the Land, to learn תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי said: There was a story with יוסף הכהן, who followed his teacher to צידון to learn תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי brings a real-life case to back up what he just said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף was a כהן, and צידון is outside ארץ ישראל. He still went there to stay with his own teacher. This shows a כהן may leave to learn from the teacher who is right for him.

keyTerms.meaning: A story, an actual case that happened

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei said:
There was an incident with Yosef the priest

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָלַךְ אַחַר רַבּוֹ לְצִידוֹן לִלְמוֹד תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: who followed his teacher to Sidon to learn Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּיוֹסֵף הַכֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוסי's opinion from step 15.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוסי's view that a כהן may leave the Land to learn even when teachers are available.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of יוסף הכהן going to צידון after his teacher.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה is like רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן decides the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The practical rule is that a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה even if teachers exist in the Land. This settles the dispute inside the ברייתא. The גמרא returns to the larger question from step 10, whether the רבנן argue with רבי נתן, in steps 18-19.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן may become impure (from rabbinic impurity) to fight gentiles in court, to learn תורה, or to marry. The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: he may go to learn even if teachers are available at home.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute presented in steps 14-16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי יוסי: a כהן may leave ארץ ישראל to learn תורה even when he could learn in the Land.

steps.title: So the Rabbis do disagree with Rabbi Natan
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that allows buying at a gentile fair seems to prove that the רבנן disagree with רבי נתן.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows that they disagree!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא that allowed buying animals and property at a gentile fair. It points out that this seems to clash with רבי נתן, who forbade buying there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נתן forbade buying at the fair because the tax collected goes to the idol. The ברייתא allows buying there, so it looks like the רבנן argue with him. That would make רבי נתן a lone opinion, which challenges רבי יוחנן's position that they agree.

keyTerms.meaning: It follows / apparently, from this we see
A gentile fair or market, often linked to idol worship

phrases.english: It follows that they disagree!
phrases.notes: "They" means the רבנן of this ברייתא versus רבי נתן, who forbade buying at the fair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about a כהן leaving the Land, the גמרא returns to the main issue of the fair.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's position that the רבנן do not argue with רבי נתן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא permits buying at the fair, but רבי נתן forbids it. So the two must disagree.

steps.title: Merchant versus homeowner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that there is no disagreement. רבי נתן speaks of buying from a merchant who pays tax to the idol, and the ברייתא speaks of buying from a private homeowner who pays no tax.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can tell you: really, they do not disagree. It is no difficulty. Here, the case is one who buys from a merchant, from whom they take a tax. There, the case is one who buys from a homeowner, from whom they take no tax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by showing that the two sources are talking about two different sellers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with buying at the fair is the tax that benefits the idol. A merchant pays that tax, so buying from him is forbidden, as רבי נתן said. A private homeowner pays no tax, so buying from him is allowed, as the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: A private homeowner, not a professional seller

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יוחנן, buying at a gentile fair is forbidden only from a merchant who pays the idol's tax, and buying from a private homeowner is allowed. So in his view רבי נתן and the רבנן agree, while ריש לקיש holds that they disagree.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan can say to you:
Really, they do not disagree,
and it is not difficult:
here, it is about one who buys from a merchant,
phrases.notes: "Here" is רבי נתן, who forbids buying.

phrases.english: since they take a tax from him;
there, it is about one who buys from a homeowner,
phrases.notes: "There" is the ברייתא that allows buying at the fair.

phrases.english: since they do not take a tax from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לְעוֹלָם לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): different kinds of sellers
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא and רבי נתן seem to rule differently on the same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: They speak of different sellers, a tax-paying merchant versus a homeowner, so they do not disagree.

steps.title: Destroying the animal causes it suffering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי נתן's ברייתא, which says an animal bought at the fair must be destroyed. It then asks how that fits with the ban on causing animals pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: an animal should be destroyed. But there is the concern of suffering to animals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the earlier ברייתא and challenges it. The challenge is that destroying the animal would cause it pain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that an animal bought from the forbidden fair must undergo עיקור, which means maiming it. But the Torah cares about צער בעלי חיים. How can the ברייתא require something that hurts the animal?

keyTerms.meaning: It should be destroyed (maimed so it is useless)

phrases.english: The Master said: an animal should be destroyed.
phrases.notes: This quotes the ברייתא of רבי נתן about something bought at the forbidden fair.

phrases.english: But there is the problem of suffering to animals!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: בְּהֵמָה תֵּיעָקֵר. וְהָא אִיכָּא צַעַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the fair question to the details of רבי נתן's ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the animal must be destroyed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Maiming an animal causes it pain, which seems to go against צער בעלי חיים.

steps.title: The Torah itself commanded maiming horses
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers from the פסוק where ה׳ told יהושע to maim the enemy's horses.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The Merciful One said, "You shall maim their horses."
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge by bringing a פסוק that commands maiming animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If ה׳ told יהושע to maim horses, then עיקור is allowed when there is a real need. This holds even though it causes the animal pain. Here the need is to keep away from anything tied to עבודה זרה.

keyTerms.meaning: "The Merciful One": ה׳, speaking through the Torah or a פסוק
Maiming an animal so it cannot be used

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The Merciful One said: "You shall maim their horses."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from a פסוק that the act is allowed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: צער בעלי חיים should forbid maiming the animal.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah itself commanded עיקור of horses, so it is allowed when needed.

steps.title: How the animal is destroyed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's definition of עיקור: cutting the hooves from the knee down.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: What is עיקור? One cuts its hooves from the knee and below.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of רבי נתן's ברייתא, which defines how עיקור is done. This sets up a contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here עיקור means a physical act of cutting the animal's lower legs. This makes the animal useless, but it does not kill it right away. This definition is what the next ברייתא will be compared against.

keyTerms.meaning: The knee joint of the animal

phrases.english: The Master said: And what is destroying?
One cuts off its hooves
from the knee and below.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues analyzing רבי נתן's ברייתא, now its definition of עיקור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עיקור means cutting the animal's hooves from the knee down.

steps.title: A contrasting source about הקדש today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא about הקדש nowadays. That ברייתא also requires עיקור of an animal, and it will be compared with the definition just given.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a contradiction was raised: One may not consecrate, dedicate as חרם, or make an ערכין vow in our times. And if one did consecrate, dedicate, or vow an ערך, an animal should be destroyed, and produce, garments, and vessels...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing a ברייתא that will clash with the definition of עיקור from step 22. The actual clash comes in the lines right after this, so this step is setting up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a בית המקדש, we should not make things holy, because holy items might be misused. If someone did, a holy animal must undergo עיקור, and other items get their own treatment. The challenge will come from how this ברייתא carries out the עיקור.

keyTerms.meaning: "And they contrasted": introduces a source that contradicts
Consecrating something to the בית המקדש (הקדש)
Vowing the set value (ערכין) of a person to the בית המקדש
In our times, without the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not finish the contradiction. The point of conflict, how this ברייתא does the עיקור, comes in the next lines of the גמרא.

phrases.english: And a contradiction was raised:
One may not consecrate, and one may not dedicate as חרם,
and one may not make value vows in our times,
and if one did consecrate, dedicate, or make a value vow,
an animal should be destroyed,
produce, garments, and vessels...

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to test the definition of עיקור given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The definition of עיקור as cutting the hooves from the knee down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ברייתא also requires עיקור of an animal, and its method will be compared against this definition in the lines that follow.
